findings.title: The cosmic all as a servant answer to sonship
findings.claim: Every being in the heavens and earth is encompassed as arriving before al-Rahman in servant status; beside the supplied child-claim passages, that shared dependence is the universal counterpart to an exceptional offspring relation.
findings.mechanism: The focus carriers are kull, the active participle ati, al-Rahman, and the circumstantial abd status. In 2:116 a child claim is followed by the whole heavens-earth domain belonging to God and universal devotion; 21:26 names al-Rahman in a child claim before recasting the referents as honored servants; 3:83 includes willing and unwilling submission; 27:87 depicts all arriving humbled after the trumpet. These wider triggers meet the focus's totality, arrival, name, and servant-state, making the universal count an explicit dependent relation and keeping eschatological movement and relational presentation together.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hear each member of the cosmic all as included in the same dependent relation, rather than treating servanthood as an isolated label for one figure. The 21:26 parallel also shows that servant status can coexist with honor.
findings.containment: The 21:26 honor is stated for its referents and is not generalized to every being; 2:116 and 3:83 do not assign everyone the same fate. The connection at 27:87 makes an end-time arrival available but does not fix the physical route or chronology of 19:93. The owned-person facet is applied analogically to creaturely dependence, not human legal sale, and no literal divine parenthood or one-at-a-time procession is claimed.

findings.title: Shared servant status, differentiated reception
findings.claim: The focus's servant classification can be universal while the wider surah differentiates the promises and judgment received by particular servants.

In 19:61 the Merciful promises gardens to His servants, 19:63 specifies inheritance of the Garden for the God-fearing among them, and 19:69 singles out the most rebellious from each group.
